messages:
priya: Heads-up — escalation from customer ACME (Private deployment us-west-2). After switching to Direct Connect they see intermittent 5xx from the API and lots of TLS handshake failures. Customer says it started right after the DX cutover.

sam_cust: attaching curl -v from their app node: 
```
* curl -v https://private-api.acme.internal/health
* > SSL: certificate subject CN=api.redwood.com
* * Hostname 'private-api.acme.internal' doesn't match certificate's altnames
* * Closing connection 0
* curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject CN=api.redwood.com
```

priya: they also see repeated 503s in logs and a few x509 errors in our control plane logs referencing acme's private hostname.

jordan: curious — that looks like DNS resolving to our public LB (api.redwood.com) instead of the private control-plane endpoint. Can we get `dig` from the customer resolver and a traceroute?

sam_cust: here you go: 
```
$ dig +short private-api.acme.internal @10.1.2.2
34.210.55.66
```
(the 34.210.55.66 is one of our public ELB IPs)

maya: thanks. Can they `curl --resolve private-api.acme.internal:443:10.0.5.12 https://private-api.acme.internal/health` using the private IP we gave them? that will prove if TLS works when DNS points to the private path.

sam_cust: tried that — with --resolve pointing to the internal VIP it returns 200 OK and the cert matches the private CN. So TLS is fine over the direct path.

kevin: ok that confirms a split-horizon DNS problem. Looks like their VPC resolver is returning public records for the internal name. Two likely causes: (1) Route53 inbound endpoint / resolver rules aren't configured to point 
private-api.acme.internal -> private IP, or (2) resolver order sends queries to public resolver first after DX BGP change.

netbot: automated alert: DX session dx-acme-1 saw route priority change at 2026-03-16T18:04:12Z — default route preference flipped to internet path for 34.210.0.0/16 for ~5m.

jordan: interesting — if BGP pref changed while they were updating resolver config it could cause some queries to prefer the public path. Also check their firewall/egress allowlist — if queries hit public LB but egress blocks TLS to public IPs, the handshake could fail mid-flight.

priya: customer confirms they have an egress allowlist during migration that only allows 10.0.0.0/8 and the new DX routes for our private subnet, but they did not include our public ELB IPs. When queries resolve to public IPs, traffic may be dropped or hairpinned through a proxy with mismatched SNI.

kevin: ask them to run `tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 443` during a failed request. If we're seeing ClientHello but no ServerHello or RST from a firewall, that's a drop. If server replies with a cert for api.redwood.com that's DNS issue.

sam_cust: tcpdump snippet: 
```
12:01:23.123456 IP 10.0.5.12.54321 > 34.210.55.66.443: Flags [S], seq 0
12:01:23.223456 IP 10.0.5.12.54321 > 34.210.55.66.443: Flags [P.], ack 1
12:01:23.323456 IP 34.210.55.66.443 > 10.0.5.12.54321: Flags [R.], seq 0, ack 1
```
RST from the public IP within ~200ms.

jordan: RST from the public side — likely a proxy or LB refusing the Host header/SNI mismatch, or our public ELB is sending RST because SNI doesn't match expected cert set. But the core issue remains DNS/resolver misconfiguration.

maya: remediation steps we should recommend to customer: 
1) Add Route53 resolver inbound endpoint + rule to resolve private-api.acme.internal -> private VIP.
2) Ensure VPC DNS resolver order prefers the Route53 inbound endpoint for `acme.internal` zone.
3) Temporarily allow egress to our public ELB IPs (34.210.55.0/24) during migration so failed queries can still complete while DNS stabilizes.
4) Verify by `curl --resolve` test and `openssl s_client -connect <private-ip>:443 -servername private-api.acme.internal` (should show cert with CN=private-api.acme.internal).

kevin: add: check their on-prem resolver caches too — if they have hybrid DNS caching appliances they may be serving stale public answers. Flushing cache helps.

priya: customer applied the resolver inbound endpoint and updated rule. They also added temporary egress allow for 34.210.55.0/24. After that traffic to private-api.acme.internal resolves to 10.0.5.12 and errors stopped.

sam_cust: final note from customer — they saw a small window (~3 minutes) of failed requests during the change; everything green after. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

jordan: closing loop — root cause: split-horizon DNS/resolver ordering after Direct Connect cutover caused private hostname to resolve to our public ELB; combined with egress allowlist and SNI mismatch produced TLS handshakes/5xx. Remediation = fix resolver rules + temporary egress exceptions and cache flush.

maya: I'll add a KB with the exact checks and commands (dig, curl --resolve, openssl s_client, tcpdump, Route53 inbound endpoint checklist) so support can run this faster next time.

priya: thanks team. Marking escalated ticket as resolved and will follow up with the customer for post-mortem.
